purpose: Redo the 139 Dossier subjects whose deep dives failed: fill in article and news, then a fixed deep dive each, most prominent first.

how_to_start.first_message: Read /home/ejb/Forge/apps/dossier/haiku-batch-manifest.json and follow the instructions in its prompt field.

prompt:
You are running a batch job for Dossier, a local research app on this laptop (code in ~/Forge/apps/dossier, backend at http://127.0.0.1:8437, research data on the AN3 USB drive). This file is your manifest. It holds your instructions (this prompt), ready-made commands and scripts, and the list of subjects with a status for each. It is also the progress record: if the session or the laptop crashes, the next session reads it and carries on from the statuses.

Background. 139 subjects were deep-dived while Jan (the local AI) was switched off or failing, so they hold no claims, and 62 of them also have no full article. The pipeline was fixed on 2026-09-15: a failed extraction is now retried and reported instead of being passed off as done. Your job is to give these 139 subjects a proper pass, most prominent first. The app does all of the research. You only start it, watch it cheaply, and record the results. Never write research content yourself.

Steps.
1. Preflight. Run commands.preflight. The backend must answer 200, AN3 must be mounted, and history must not be running. If the backend does not answer, run commands.start_backend once and check again. If AN3 is missing, add a session_log entry saying so and stop.
2. Check that Jan is free. Run commands.jan_busy. A number above 0 means another program is using Jan right now. In that case run commands.jan_busy_wait in the background; if it reports Jan still busy, add a session_log entry and stop. Never restart Jan, kill llama-server or change Jan's settings - Jan is shared with other sessions.
3. Fill in articles and news. Run scripts.fill_in in the background, using commands.run_script with NAME replaced by fill_in. It works through every subject whose fill_in is "pending", one at a time, and saves into this file after each. Expect roughly 10 to 40 minutes. Wait for the background completion notification; do not check on it in between.
4. Queue the deep dives. Run scripts.queue_deep_dives in the foreground (commands.run_script with NAME = queue_deep_dives; under a minute). It creates the queue named in queue_name with "redo subjects already held" switched on, makes it the active queue, queues every subject whose deep_dive is still "pending" and starts it. It leaves the older paused queues alone.
5. Watch the first results without polling. Run commands.run_wait_script in the background. It returns after 4 subjects finish or 90 minutes pass. Then run scripts.record (commands.run_script with NAME = record), which copies each finished job's result into this file.
6. Judge the first results. Good: at least one finished deep dive reads "done: +N claims" with N above 0. Bad: every finished one has +0 claims, or the failures mention Jan being unreachable. If bad, run commands.pause_queue, add a session_log entry explaining what you saw, and stop.
7. If good, leave the queue running. It works unattended for roughly a day (each deep dive takes about 25 minutes, four at a time); the backend releases Jan's memory when idle and writes ~/Forge/outputs/dossier-manifest.json every 5 minutes. Add a session_log entry (time, what ran, the counts, anything odd), then finish with a short plain report to the user: how many subjects were filled in, how many deep dives were queued, what the first results showed, and how to check progress later (the Jobs tab in Dossier, or a new session running scripts.record).

Resuming after a crash or in a later session. Read session_log and the statuses first. If any fill_in is still "pending", redo step 3 (it skips finished ones). If queue_id is already set, do not make another queue: scripts.queue_deep_dives re-activates that queue and only queues subjects still "pending". Then continue from step 5. To check on a running batch, just run step 5's record script and report.

Rules.
- Edit only this manifest file, and only while none of the scripts is running, because they save into it. Add new session_log entries; do not rewrite old ones.
- Do not edit any code, tests, WIP.md or README.md, and do not install anything.
- Do not delete queues, subjects or files. Do not run Fill in history for the whole library. Do not start the older queues.
- Do not use subagents, /loop, or repeated short sleep-and-check commands. Wait on background task notifications instead.
- Keep your messages short. Do not read the app's source code unless a script fails and its error text alone does not explain why.
- If anything unexpected happens, add a session_log entry describing it and stop, rather than improvising a fix.
queue_name: Haiku batch: redo failed deep dives

commands.preflight: curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "backend answered %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/queue; test -f /run/media/ejb/AN3/DossierData/index.json && echo "AN3 mounted" || echo "AN3 missing"; curl -s -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/history | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('history running:', json.load(sys.stdin).get('running'))"; curl -s -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/queue | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('active queue:', d['active_queue']['name'], d['counts'], 'paused:', d['paused'])"; free -m | awk 'NR==2{print "available memory MB:", $7}'
commands.start_backend: cd /home/ejb/Forge/apps/dossier && FORGE_SHARED_DIR=/home/ejb/Forge/shared setsid nohup .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn web_app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8437 >> /home/ejb/Forge/outputs/dossier.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -m 1 http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/queue >/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "backend answered %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/queue
commands.jan_busy: cd /home/ejb/Forge/apps/dossier && .venv/bin/python -c "import janidle, time; a = janidle.model_ticks(); time.sleep(20); b = janidle.model_ticks(); print('CPU ticks used in 20 s per loaded model:', {k: b.get(k, 0) - v for k, v in a.items()} or 'no models loaded')"
commands.jan_busy_wait:
cd /home/ejb/Forge/apps/dossier && .venv/bin/python -c "import janidle, time, sys
end = time.time() + 600
while time.time() < end:
    a = janidle.model_ticks(); time.sleep(20); b = janidle.model_ticks()
    if not any(b.get(k, 0) - v for k, v in a.items()):
        print('Jan is free'); sys.exit(0)
print('Jan still busy after 10 minutes'); sys.exit(1)"
commands.pause_queue: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8437/api/queue/pause | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('paused:', d['paused'], d['counts'])"
